scores.label: A
scores.note: 1 'harsh' means severe, not dangerous, and drops the danger the sentence turns on; 7 'very threatening conditions' reads as menacing, the wrong sense; 8 'toxic' narrows the meaning to poison and is slangy; 9 'unpleasant' weakens the claim; the best words (5, 6) are buried

scores.label: B
scores.note: 5 'threatening' reads as menacing, the wrong sense; 6 'hostile' is the wrong sense for factory conditions; 7 'unfavorable' weakens the claim; 8 'threatening conditions' gives 'conditions were very threatening conditions', which is ungrammatical; 10 'very potentially harmful' is ungrammatical and adds a hedge

scores.label: C
scores.note: 6 'dreadful' means awful and loses the danger; 8 'very hazard-filled' is an odd coinage; 9 'very inherently unsafe' and 10 'very extremely perilous' are ungrammatical after 'very'
